newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia chocolate demand to swell by 2000 - Flemings.
newsitem.headline: Russia chocolate demand to swell by 2000 - Flemings.

text.p: Russia's chocolate confectionery market is forecast to grow 34 percent between 1996 and 2000 and its sugar confectionery industry is set to increase by 21 percent over the same period, an industry report said.
"Both chocolate and sugar confectionery markets are expected to grow significantly in the next five years," the report, published by Robert Fleming Securities Ltd, said.

The report forecast Russian chocolate confectionery consumption at 511,000 tonnes by 2000 against 381,000 tonnes in 1996. It said sugar confectionery demand would rise to 937,000 tonnes in 2000 from 777,000 tonnes in 1996.
Flemings said the recovery in chocolate confectionery consumption would be closely linked to economic growth.
"Chocolate sweets are considered a luxury food product and their consumption is more geared to GDP and real income growth," the report said.
"Flemings is positive on Russian economic development in the medium to long term, and we believe that the sector will benefit from the economic upturn."

Imports of finished chocolate confectionery goods are likely to fall in the next few years, as they will be unable to sustain competition from improving Russian-based producers, which have a cost advantage.
Flemings also noted the shift by some international confectionery groups to produce from local factories.

The report said Red October, Russia's biggest confectioner, had an eight percent share of the country's confectionery market, putting it in second place behind Mars of the United States, which has a 10 percent slice.
Flemings said data on confectionery consumption trends and confectionery market share in Russia in the report were taken from market research company ERC Statistics International.
